quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report (consolidated, continuing operations after the copper-foil divestment): Q2 2026 revenue KRW 101,870,141,988 vs KRW 77,768,740,670 in Q2 2025; Q2 operating loss KRW 21,675,841,067 vs KRW 20,837,021,196. H1 2026 revenue KRW 189,933,191,397 vs KRW 167,291,014,449; H1 operating loss KRW 53,677,530,774 vs KRW 41,276,701,309; H1 net income KRW 56,373,532,837 including a profit from discontinued operations of KRW 96,072,019,794 (continuing-operations loss KRW 39,698,486,957). H1 mix (KRW million, incl. inter-segment sales): battery foil 136,679 (71.96%), OLED 49,534 (26.08%), advanced materials 9,894 (5.21%), eliminations -6,174. Segment operating result: battery foil loss KRW 56,158M, OLED profit KRW 1,425M, advanced materials profit KRW 872M. Revenue by location of the selling entity: Korea KRW 51,875M, Europe KRW 128,380M, Asia etc. KRW 9,678M. FY2025 restated reference: revenue KRW 309,984M, operating loss KRW 81,180M.

Copper-foil business divested: the half-year report states the sale of Circuit Foil Luxembourg S.a.r.l. (CFL), the subsidiary running the copper-foil business, together with its units Circuit Foil Asia Pacific (Zhangjiagang), Circuit Foil Asia Pacific (Hong Kong) and Circuit Foil Trading Inc., was approved by the board on 2026-01-20 and completed on 2026-04-28 (all 1,402,873 CFL shares held by Volta Energy Solutions S.a.r.l.); the buyer is not named in the report. CFL is now reported as a discontinued operation: its H1 2026 revenue of KRW 138,146M (H1 2025: KRW 134,177M) and the Luxembourg site's capacity and purchases are excluded from the continuing figures, and prior periods were restated. The remaining business consists of battery foil (Hungary, Canada under construction), OLED materials and advanced materials.
quarterly_data.figure: CFL copper-foil business sold, completed 04-28-2026; CFL H1 2026 revenue KRW 138,146M now discontinued

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity, utilisation and capex: the Hungary battery-foil plant had H1 2026 capacity of 15,222 tonnes, output of 8,823 tonnes and average utilisation of 58.0% (FY2025: 21,874 t capacity, 63.3%; FY2024: 82.2%). The Iksan OLED organic-materials plant had capacity of 8,717 kg, output of 2,365 kg and 27.1% utilisation, which the company attributes to fewer operating days while moving to the newly completed Hamyeol plant. The company is building a battery-foil plant in Granby, Quebec, Canada with 25 thousand tonnes of annual capacity, targeting mass production in 2027, and plans total battery-foil capacity of 100 thousand tonnes; subsidiary Solus ITech plans to expand capacity to 103 tonnes by 2027. H1 investment was KRW 73,571M strategic (land and building expansion) and KRW 4,082M maintenance; PP&E purchases KRW 208,201,480,315; construction in progress KRW 1,072,322M and PP&E purchase commitments KRW 531,586M at period end.
quarterly_data.figure: Hungary battery foil 15,222 t capacity, 8,823 t output, 58.0% utilisation; OLED plant 27.1%; Canada 25 thousand t/yr plant targeting 2027; PP&E commitments KRW 531,586M

quarterly_data.signal: Customers and suppliers: consolidated H1 revenue from customers above the disclosure threshold (names undisclosed) was customer A KRW 66,366M, customer B KRW 39,016M and customer C KRW 35,593M (H1 2025: KRW 68,940M, KRW 46,760M, KRW 31,351M). Battery foil has been supplied since 2020 under medium- to long-term supply contracts with global battery-cell makers and EV makers, with further contracts added (terms confidential); OLED materials are sold under master agreements with major domestic and overseas OLED display makers against purchase orders. Main raw material for battery foil is copper scrap bought from copper recyclers and traders (KRW 71,797M in H1); OLED/advanced-materials raw materials are bought from Inco Co. and JH Trade among others (KRW 16,163M for mass production). The parent has agreed to buy all high-refractive fillers and low-dielectric TFE products made by subsidiary Solus ITech.
quarterly_data.figure: Customer A KRW 66,366M, B KRW 39,016M, C KRW 35,593M in H1 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook stated in the half-year report: the company aims to widen battery-foil market share in EVs, expand entry into ESS battery foil and develop high-end foil for next-generation batteries (silicon anodes, solid-state), citing ESS market growth of over 22% a year from 2025 to 2029 driven partly by AI and data-center power demand. It presents battery-foil demand of 622 thousand tonnes in 2025 rising to 1,170 thousand tonnes in 2029 and a global OLED materials market of about KRW 1.2 trillion in 2025 expected to exceed KRW 1.5 trillion by 2030 (company figures). It gives its domestic battery-foil market share as 31% in 2025 and its global OLED-materials share as 10%. In OLED it is pursuing phosphorescent green host and non-emissive materials alongside HBL/ETL common-layer materials; R&D spend KRW 3,010M (1.58% of revenue).
quarterly_data.figure: Canada plant mass production target 2027; ESS CAGR over 22% (2025-2029); domestic battery-foil share 31% (2025)
